I have farmed these 6 mu in Quzhou for 40 years, and finishing high school taught me to keep records and think about nutrient balance instead of just copying my neighbors. Our land is loamy but tired from decades of vegetables, so I pay attention to potassium and organic matter. I talk to the seed dealer, I read the county extension leaflets, and my son checks prices on his phone. My core system is cabbage-maize-cabbage on 5 mu because that is what earns the money, and I keep small plots near the house: 0.4 mu of chili, 0.3 mu of kidney bean, and 0.3 mu of winter spinach. I start from last year’s results and adjust. My spring cabbage gave 4,800 kg per mu last year but the heads were a bit loose, so this year I will push nitrogen to 28 kg per mu and add 2,000 kg of fermented chicken manure as a base. I use hybrid F1 cabbage seedlings from the dealer in town. I will apply 70 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before transplanting, then topdress three times with urea. I irrigate five times and spray four times for diamondback moth and downy mildew. For summer maize I plant Zhengdan 958 right after the cabbage comes off in June; last year I only got 520 kg per mu because I skimped on the third irrigation at filling, so this year I will irrigate three times and apply 20 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. Autumn cabbage goes in after the maize comes out, 25 kg nitrogen, 9 kg phosphorus, 12 kg potassium per mu, with four irrigations and three sprays. The chili gets 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu because it is a heavy feeder and the market price is good, plus six irrigations so the fruit does not crack. Kidney bean gets 12 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu; beans make some of their own nitrogen but still need a starter. Spinach is a quick winter crop, 10 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, 5 kg potassium per mu, three irrigations. I do rotary tillage before every crop to save time and diesel. Fertilizer is expensive—urea is 120 yuan per 50 kg bag—but cabbage is my main cash crop. I would rather spend an extra 200 yuan on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. A bad cabbage year is a disaster; wasting half a bag of urea is just a cost. I hire three workers for two days at transplanting, that is 400 yuan, and my wife and I do the rest. I watch Old Wang next door: he put too much nitrogen on his maize last year and it lodged, so I am keeping maize at 20 kg nitrogen and putting the extra money into cabbage instead.
